benchmark.name: Single-binary deep stereo SLAM: in-process ONNX vs file-based front-end, end-to-end wall-clock (EuRoC MH_03_medium)
benchmark.protocol: Same rectified EuRoC MH_03_medium 2700-frame stereo image stream driven through the same Rust binary (stereo_vo_external_deep_files) and the same loop-closure/BA configuration (--online-ba --online-ba-window 10 --online-ba-history 20 --loop-closure --loop-min-frame-gap 200 --loop-two-view-ba --loop-edge-information), varying only where features and matches come from: --in-process-onnx computes SuperPoint + LightGlue per frame in-process via ONNX Runtime (GPU); the file-based comparator reads pre-exported --features-dir features (Python + PyTorch export, about 30 GB on disk). Both trajectories are scored with the same evo_ape against the timestamped Vicon/Leica ground truth.

command.raw: stereo_vo_external_deep_files --images-dir /tmp/MH_03_rect --calib /tmp/MH_03_rect/calib.txt --features-dir /tmp/sp_lg_MH_03 --frames 2700 --online-ba --online-ba-window 10 --online-ba-history 20 --loop-closure --loop-min-frame-gap 200 --loop-two-view-ba --loop-edge-information --out-dir target/deep_slam_mh03_file_based  # documented prior GPU run invocation; NOT re-run in this session

dataset.name: EuRoC MAV
dataset.version: ASL EuRoC MAV dataset, full 2700 frames

hardware.gpu: NVIDIA CUDA GPU (same documented prior-run machine as the in-process arm; this file-based arm does not exercise the CUDA ONNX Runtime provider)
hardware.notes: Windows CUDA ONNX Runtime provider DLLs + cuDNN 9 are not set up in this session, so this GPU run is not reproduced locally; see notes/provenance below.

metrics.name: ate_sim3

notes: Phase 3 registry formalization of the existing single-binary in-process deep-stereo-SLAM end-to-end wall-clock result documented in docs/inprocess_slam_benchmark.md (EuRoC MH_03_medium, full 2700 frames). This is the file-based comparator arm: stereo_vo_external_deep_files reads pre-exported SuperPoint + LightGlue features from --features-dir, produced by a separate Python + PyTorch export pass and stored as an about-30-GB on-disk feature dump; identical downstream windowed online BA, loop closure, and pose-graph optimization as the in-process ONNX arm. PROVENANCE: this manifest formalizes a documented prior GPU run (docs/inprocess_slam_benchmark.md); it is NOT reproduced in this session. A local re-run needs Windows CUDA ONNX Runtime provider DLLs plus cuDNN 9 plus a PyTorch SuperPoint/LightGlue ONNX export, which is impractical for this evidence-formalization pass. ACCURACY CAVEAT: the two arms are NOT bit-identical. The file-based features were exported by a separate Python SuperPoint pass, so the keypoint sets differ slightly from the in-process ONNX export's own selection (top-1500 above a 0.005 score gate); given the same features, the ONNX LightGlue matches ARE bit-identical to the Python reference (1500/1500 indices agree, docs/lightglue_onnx_benchmark.md). The small ATE difference between the two arms is therefore attributable to the front-end's keypoint selection, not the matcher. Both arms land within about 2.4x of ORB-SLAM3 on this flight.
